title: Efficient Recycling Subspace Truncation Method for Periodic Small-Signal Analysis
problem: Krylov subspace recycling for periodic small-signal RF analysis accelerates simulation but increasing memory cost becomes a bottleneck in large-scale designs; restarting loses recycling benefits.
motivation: RF simulation at multiple frequency points is time-consuming; memory limitations force restart compromising efficiency gains from recycling.
method: The method accelerates RF circuit simulation by recycling old calculation results from previous cycles—a technique that normally requires storing everything but threatens memory limits in large designs. Instead, it intelligently trims the stored results using a Floquet-based strategy, keeping only the most valuable ones (Floquet theory mathematically describes systems that repeat periodically). It also selects optimal starting points for each simulation cycle to minimize iterations needed.
key_novelty: Using Floquet theory to decide which recycled calculation results to keep and which to discard, reducing memory use in periodic circuit simulations.
contributions: Recycling subspace truncation framework for periodic small-signal analysis
